conviction_note: Roughly balanced. On the plus side: GM's beat-and-raise record (the last four prints closed up +4.9, +1.3, +8.75 and +14.9), a CFO who said warranty benefits fall mostly in Q3 and that GM would 'bank' its first-half beats, and a buyback that is still running. On the minus side, all of it proxy or risk evidence: record fuel prices hitting the truck/SUV used values that GM Financial's lease book depends on, an NHTSA engineering analysis covering ~998k L87 V8 vehicles opened a month before GM's Q3 warranty-accrual review, and GM's September transaction price falling while every Detroit peer's rose. That gives p_up 53 on abs 6.5 = +0.39. The finding sum (-0.1) and the scaled number (+0.39) differ only in sign noise: both say no edge.
bar: Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of about $3.52-3.61 on revenue of about $48.2-48.7bn. Zacks has $3.52 / $48.24bn (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/general-motors-gm-q3-earnings-121523736.html, 2026-10-15). TradingKey has $3.52 / $48.7bn (https://www.tradingkey.com/analysis/stocks/us-stocks/262220891-general-motors-stock-forecast-q3-earnings-triangle-breakout-october-17-2026-tradingkey). Benzinga Pro has $3.60 and MarketBeat $3.70 (https://www.indmoney.com/blog/us-stocks/general-motors-q3-earnings-preview). Two sources agree within about 2.5%, so the bar is usable. Zacks segment estimates: GMNA $3.28bn (year-ago $2.51bn), GM Financial $775M (year-ago $804M), GMI $143.6M (year-ago $226M). Company FY2026 guide, raised in July: EBIT-adj $14-16bn, adj EPS $12-14, adj auto FCF $9.5-11.5bn (https://www.xtb.com/int/market-analysis/news-and-research/general-motors-shares-down-despite-solid-earnings-report). H1 EBIT-adj was $8.19bn, so the guide implies $5.8-7.8bn for H2. A Q3 consensus around $3.55 EPS (about $3.9bn EBIT) already sits above the guide midpoint's quarterly run-rate, so the market expects the range to be raised or at least held at the top.
positioning_check: Short interest is about 24.5M shares at the 2026-07-15 FINRA settlement, roughly 4.1 days to cover (https://equibles.com/stocks/gm/shortinterest). Benzinga puts it at 2.3-3.0% of float (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/GM/sentiment). No settlement after July was found. Not a crowded short. Baseline skew is +0.38 vol points (balanced), put/call OI 0.76, event-implied move 5.07% (straddle 5.76%). Spot $82.41: -1.83% over 20 days, 8.7% below the 52-week high, +42% off the low. The sell-side trimmed targets into the print: per TradingKey, JPMorgan cut to $110 from $120 on 10-12 and UBS to $112 from $114. A separate search could not confirm the JPM cut. Average target is about $100-101.

findings.finding: On the Q2 call (2026-07-21) the CFO guided H2 shape. Warranty benefits fall mostly in Q3, when GM also reviews accrual rates. Q4 will be weaker than normal seasonality (full-size truck launch costs, about a 35k-unit year-over-year volume headwind). GM would 'bank what we've sort of earned ahead of expectations in the first half'. With H1 EBIT-adj at $8.19bn against a $14-16bn FY range, a Q3 near the $3.9bn consensus puts nine months at about $12bn, so a raise of at least the low end of the range is mechanically likely. That is GM's fourth consecutive raise-type print, and the market expects one.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Raise or hold-high prints: 2025-10-21 +14.86% (beat and raise), 2026-01-27 +8.75% (2026 guide plus buyback), 2026-04-28 +1.27% (raise on IEEPA relief), 2026-07-21 +4.91% (second raise; -2% pre-market on lower GAAP net income guide). The 2025-07-22 print, with no raise and heavy tariff cost, fell -8.12%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. Previews already ask for a 'third raise' (TradingKey), and consensus Q3 EPS sits above the guide-midpoint run-rate. What is less priced is how big the raise can be. Q4 is flagged as seasonally weak, so a raise is likely to be modest (low end up rather than the top), and a hold would read as a miss against a consensus that has already embedded one. Fully priced would look like a stock trading through the 52-week high into the print; instead it sits 8.7% below it with a balanced skew.
findings.independence: TradingKey preview (2026-10-17) expects a third raise and notes that consensus EPS is $3.52 against Q2's $3.57 actual: https://www.tradingkey.com/analysis/stocks/us-stocks/262220891-general-motors-stock-forecast-q3-earnings-triangle-breakout-october-17-2026-tradingkey. Shares the H1 arithmetic with the bar field.

findings.finding: NHTSA opened Engineering Analysis EA26005 on 2026-08-21. It covers 997,743 MY2021-2026 vehicles with the 6.2L L87 V8 (Silverado 1500, Sierra 1500, Tahoe, Suburban, Yukon, Escalade). The existing recall covers 597,630 vehicles. NHTSA cites 499 failures after the oil-change remedy and 191 failures in engines built after May 2024, outside the recall population; GM itself reported 6,953 such complaints. GM has said L87 cost about $500M so far. The probe opened after the July call on which GM raised its warranty improvement to $1-1.5bn and said Q3 is when accrual rates are reviewed. That puts upside risk on the Q3 warranty accrual, on GM's most profitable nameplates, against a Q3 the consensus expects to carry the warranty benefit.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Warranty was GM's second-largest headwind in Q2 2025, when L87 added about $300M year over year, and the 2025-07-22 print fell -8.12% (tariffs were the main driver). No print has turned on warranty alone.
findings.why_not_priced: Safety-probe news ran in the auto trade press in August. None of the October previews (Zacks, TradingKey, INDmoney) mention it, and the July call's Q3 warranty benefit is still the street's assumption (warranty improvement raised to $1-1.5bn, $500M realised in H1). If it were priced, previews would carry a warranty-accrual risk line and the Q3 EPS bar would have come down. It moved -0.2% in 30 days per Zacks.
findings.independence: Separate reporting of the same EA scope (997,743 vehicles, 2021-2026): https://www.galvnews.com/news_reuters/nation/gm-engine-recall-investigation-just-got-a-whole-lot-bigger/article_12d54824-108d-5714-afaa-4081886d00f5.html. The Q3 accrual-review timing comes from the Q2 transcript, the same document as the guidance finding.

findings.finding: Cox's Q3 Manheim report (2026-10-07): wholesale values for vehicles rated under 15 mpg are down 15% since January, and 15-19 mpg vehicles are down almost 9%, while 40+ mpg vehicles are up 9.9%. The overall index is down 0.6% year over year, Cox cut its 2026 forecast to +0.2% from +2%, and pickups and SUVs are below year-ago. GM Financial's lease book is weighted to GM trucks and SUVs, so residual and remarketing gains are under pressure. GMF earned $600M EBT-adj in Q2, and Zacks has $775M for Q3, a 29% sequential rebound.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: GM Financial has not been the swing line on any of the last seven prints. GMF is about $0.6-0.8bn of quarterly EBT against $3.9bn EBIT-adj, so a $100-150M shortfall is about 3-4% of EPS.
findings.why_not_priced: The headline Manheim number (-0.6% year over year) looks benign; the fuel-economy split that hits GMF's specific collateral sits in Cox's body text. GMF's FY guide of $2.5-3.0bn was maintained in July and leaves room for $0.6-0.86bn a quarter, so the $775M segment estimate looks un-cut. This is a proxy: GM has not quantified any residual hit.
findings.independence: Cox's own September index page ties weaker valuations to fuel costs and record diesel prices: https://www.coxautoinc.com/insights/manheim-used-vehicle-value-index-september-2026-trends/. GMF's Q2 figure comes from the Q2 transcript (https://www.webull.com/news/15265646602101760). The 10-Q shows the GMF loan-loss allowance up to 3.1% of receivables from 2.9%.

findings.finding: GM's July guide 'assumes no material Middle East escalation'. Since then US gasoline has stayed above $4 for a record 158 days: September set a record monthly average and AAA had $4.33 on 2026-10-14. Industry ICE incentives in September were up 31.6% year over year to $3,319 a unit (J.D. Power, via Mercer). GM's Q3 large SUVs (Tahoe, Suburban) declined while Trax and Trailblazer rose. Together this is a forward risk to truck/SUV mix and pricing in the Q4 and 2027 outlook. Q3 itself is cushioned by Silverado 1500 +13.3%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: GM's CFO played down gas-price demand effects in Q1 2026 and Barra said the shift to smaller vehicles 'is just not happening' on the Q2 call. The stock rose on both prints, so this line has not yet cost GM a reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: fuel prices are front-page news and the stock is 8.7% off its high. The incremental part is that the guide's own stated assumption has arguably been breached since July, so Q4 commentary on large-vehicle mix and incentives could temper a raise. Fully priced would look like a put skew; the skew is balanced.
findings.independence: J.D. Power September incentive data via Mercer Capital (2026-10-15): https://mercercapital.com/insights/blogs/auto-dealer-valuation-insights-blog/2026/september-2026-saar/. WSJ syndication on GM's Q3 large-SUV declines: https://investnews.com.br/the-wall-street-journal/gasolina-mais-cara-faz-americanos-voltarem-a-sedas-e-suvs-compactos/amp/. This is macro-to-company transmission and a proxy.

findings.finding: Kelley Blue Book, September 2026: GM's average transaction price (before incentives) was $54,468, -0.9% year over year (Chevrolet -0.2%, GMC -0.7%, Buick -0.3%, Cadillac +6.2%). Ford was +3.8%, Stellantis +6.7%, Toyota +4.6%, and the industry +0.7%. Full-size pickup segment ATP was +1.5% and full-size SUV +3.8%, so GM is lagging its own segments.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Pricing has been a tailwind GM highlighted on the last two prints, both of which rose. No print has turned on a pricing miss.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely inside what GM guided: FY pricing of about +0.5%, with H2 moderation as it laps last year's model-year 2026 increases. Part of the year-over-year drop is mix from the EV collapse. Previews quote GM's Q2 incentive discipline (4.7% of MSRP) and not the September ATP table. Small because it lands inside the guide.
findings.independence: Q2-call pricing guidance is in the same transcript as the guidance finding: https://www.webull.com/news/15265646602101760.

findings.finding: GM's Q3 2026 US deliveries were 670,974 (-5.5%). EVs fell 61.7% to 25,473 (3.8% of sales against 9.4%), so non-EV volume was roughly flat (about +2k units). Silverado 1500 rose 13.3% to 100,221 and fleet rose about 10%. Zacks has GMNA wholesale at 842k, flat year over year. Fewer loss-making EVs plus strong pickups is a positive mix for GMNA EBIT, consistent with GM's guided $1-1.5bn EV-loss improvement.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 (record EVs, deliveries +7.7%) printed a beat and raise and rose +14.86%. Q1 2026 US sales -9.7% printed a beat and rose +1.27%. Unit sales have not predicted the reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Public since 10-01, so mostly priced. The fleet-heavy mix (fleet is lower margin) and the slightly elevated $48.7bn revenue consensus are the small open questions.
findings.independence: INDmoney preview carries the same totals plus fleet +10%: https://www.indmoney.com/blog/us-stocks/general-motors-q3-earnings-preview. TradingKey has the EV share: https://www.tradingkey.com/analysis/stocks/us-stocks/262220891-general-motors-stock-forecast-q3-earnings-triangle-breakout-october-17-2026-tradingkey.

findings.finding: GM's China JVs delivered about 358,000 vehicles in Q3 2026 against roughly 470,000 in Q3 2025 (about -24% year over year, flat on Q2's ~357k), with NEVs above 60% of the mix. China equity income was about $100M in Q2. The Q2 call also said Middle East shipping disruption hurt GMI wholesales, and the Hormuz disruption has continued.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: China equity income is about $0.1bn a quarter and has not been the swing line on recent prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the Zacks GMI segment estimate is already cut to $143.6M from $226M a year ago. Flat sequential volume means little news against Q2.

findings.finding: Capital return: GM had $3.5bn left on its repurchase authorization at the end of Q2. It bought back $2.8bn and 36M shares in H1 ($2.0bn in Q2), and the CFO said GM expects to keep repurchasing consistently. A Q3 release paired with a new authorization or ASR is possible; the January 2026 print, which paired the 2026 guide with a $6bn capacity increase, rose +8.75%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-01-27 (buyback capacity +$6bn with the guide): +8.75%. 2025-02 ASR announcement: positive.
findings.why_not_priced: The remaining-capacity arithmetic ($3.5bn after a $2bn quarter leaves fewer than two quarters at that pace) is in the 10-Q and the call, not in the previews. A new authorization is a possibility, not a disclosed plan.
findings.independence: Q2 transcript, $3.5bn remaining: https://www.webull.com/news/15265646602101760. Not independent of the 10-Q arithmetic.

findings.finding: Unlike Q3 2025, when GM filed an Item 2.06 Material Impairments 8-K on 2025-10-14 ($1.6bn EV capacity charge) a week before the print, GM has filed no 8-K since the 2026-08-11 supplier-inventory facility. That is no pre-announced Q3 EV impairment, consistent with the January 2026 8-K saying 2026 EV charges would be 'significantly less' than 2025's, and the CFO saying material cash EV charges are 'substantially' complete after $2.3bn in Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: July 2026: $2.3bn of EV charges cut GAAP net income and the net income guide, and shares were -2% pre-market, but the close was +4.91% on the EBIT-adj raise. Charges below EBIT-adj have been looked through.
findings.why_not_priced: Below operating income, so sized at a fraction. Absence of a 2.06 filing is weak evidence: Item 2.06 can be satisfied in the periodic report instead.

findings.finding: Financing (8-K, 2026-08-11): GM set up a facility of up to $4.5bn outstanding through Procura Auto Parts, funded by a JPMorgan/Santander syndicate at SOFR+1.55%. It prepays key suppliers to buy and hold critical inventory for GM, booked as product financing (prepayment asset, unsecured debt). What the money buys is production continuity against supply shocks. The industry context is an automotive DRAM squeeze that Samsung Securities said could hit vehicle output from H2 2026, and GM's Micron supply agreement. It is not distress funding.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print turned on a financing event.
findings.why_not_priced: Public since August. The Q3 release may show whether it was drawn and what it protected (no Q3 production disruption reported). The answer to the financing question is 'protects output', so the sign is mildly positive or zero.

findings.finding: Commodity, logistics and DRAM costs, guided at $1.5-2.0bn for FY2026, are back-half weighted because H2 carries two quarters of higher prices. S&P Global warned automotive DRAM prices could rise 70-100% in 2026, and in June Micron said supply stays constrained 'beyond 2027'. That is a 2027 cost overhang that the Q3 call is likely to be asked about.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Cost headwinds have been in every 2026 guide, and both 2026 prints rose anyway.
findings.why_not_priced: Inside the guide, so near zero. Only a 2027 framing beyond what GM has said would matter.

findings.finding: Into the print, the sell-side trimmed targets: per TradingKey, JPMorgan cut to $110 from $120 on 10-12 and UBS to $112 from $114. One preview counts 13 downward Q3 EPS revisions in 30 days, while Zacks shows consensus down only 0.2%. The stock fell 1.13% on 10-14 to $83.05 and closed $82.41 on 10-19. A slightly lowered bar on a company that has beaten in every recent quarter is a mild positive for the beat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: GM has beaten EPS consensus on each of the last several prints (Q2 2026 $3.57 vs about $3.19-3.29).
findings.why_not_priced: Small: the target cuts are public. The JPM cut could not be confirmed by a second search (which found only July's raise to $120), so it is capped small.
findings.independence: Zacks: -0.2% 30-day revision, https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/general-motors-gm-q3-earnings-121523736.html. The two sources disagree on revision depth.

outside_window.finding: Outcome of NHTSA EA26005 (accept remedy, change inspection, or seek a broader L87 recall across ~998k vehicles). An engineering analysis typically runs months; only GM's Q3 accrual and commentary fall inside the window, and that part is filed above.

IEEPA refund CAPE Phase 3 opened 2026-10-06 for finally liquidated entries; CBP's comment period on the refund framework closes 2026-11-04. GM already booked a $0.5bn IEEPA benefit in Q1, so any further refund timing is beyond the window and below the guide.

baseline_tension: The skew is balanced (+0.38) and the 20-day run-up is slightly negative (-1.83%). The evidence is two-sided in the same way: a likely modest guidance raise against proxy-level risks to GM Financial, warranty and large-vehicle mix. Nothing here cuts against the option market.
lessons_applied: Rule 5 (proxy smaller): GM Financial residual finding -0.5 -> -0.4 and fuel/guide finding -0.6 -> -0.4. Both are macro-to-company transmission GM has not confirmed. Their weight in p_up also fell, which moved p_up 52 -> 53.

Rule 6 (inside the guide): KBB ATP finding -0.4 -> -0.2, because GM guided +0.5% FY pricing with H2 moderation. DRAM/commodity finding -0.2 -> -0.1, because it is inside the $1.5-2.0bn guided headwind.
Rule 3 (caveat reaches the number): guidance-raise finding +1.2 -> +1.0, because the raise is expected and Q4 is flagged weak, which limits its size.
L87 EA finding: -0.6 -> -0.5. The NHTSA outcome itself was moved to outside_window; only the Q3 accrual risk stays.

Rule 4 (financing): the $4.5bn inventory facility was confirmed as protecting production, not funding distress, and stays +0.1. Rules 1 and 7 changed nothing: GM's prints have paid for raises and the short is not crowded.
